headline: New York City's comptroller has urged Anthropic to delay its planned stock market listing until it deals with AI safety concerns.
score_reason: Letter is published and confirmed, involves a major AI lab and a very large pension investor; it is a request, not a binding step.
importance_line: It puts a public safety and governance question to Anthropic from the elected overseer of $325 billion of city pension money, which could shape investor expectations, but the comptroller cannot block the listing and Anthropic had not yet responded.
summary: Reuters reports, citing CNBC, that Mark Levine, New York City's elected comptroller and trustee of its pension funds, wrote on 14 Oct 2026 to Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei asking the company to pause its planned initial public offering (a first sale of shares to the public) and first set out specific audits and controls. According to PYMNTS's account of the letter, Levine cites Amodei's own call to slow the pace of AI capability gains and says IPO preparation "diverts resources and attention" from safety work.
notes: Reuters link blocked; text read on PYMNTS, which describes the letter posted by the Comptroller.
